[[Powership]] | revenue = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|2850.60|c}} (2025)[https://goashipyard.in/assets/front/public/financial-year-wise-annual-reports-pdf/Annual-Report-2024-25-English-Language.pdf"Annual Statement 2024-25 "]. | operating_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|378.64|c}} (2025) | net_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|288.44|c}} (2025) | assets = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|7335.99|c}} (2025) | equity = {{Increase}} {{INRConvert|1620.58|c}} (2025) | num_employees = {{increase}} 1386 (2025) | subsidiaries = | website = [https://goashipyard.in/ Goa Shipyard] }} '''Goa Shipyard Limited''' ('''GSL''') is a [[public sector undertaking]] for defence ship building located on the West Coast of India at [[Vasco da Gama, Goa]]. It was established in 1957, originally by the colonial government of the Portuguese in India as the "Estaleiros Navais de Goa",{{Cite web |url=http://indiannavy.nic.in/t2t2e/Trans2Trimph/chapters/5_mdl%20%26%20leander%20project.htm |title=Chapter-5 |access-date=13 March 2022 |archive-date=1 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081101174339/http://indiannavy.nic.in/t2t2e/Trans2Trimph/chapters/5_mdl%20%26%20leander%20project.htm |url-status=dead }} to build barges to be used in [[Goa]]'s growing mining industry, which took off after the establishment of India's blockade of Goa in 1955. In the wake of Portugal's defeat and unconditional surrender to India following the [[1961 Indian annexation of Goa]], it was requisitioned to manufacture warships for the [[Indian Navy]] and the [[Indian Coast Guard]]. GSL is undergoing a modernisation of its yard to adapt to the latest technology in shipbuilding. To this purpose it is negotiating with well-known shipbuilders for an arrangement to collaborate. To date it has built 167 vessels, including barges, tugs, landing craft, offshore patrol vessels and other vessels for the Indian Navy and Coast Guard and for export to countries like Yemen.{{cite web |url = https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/india/goa-sy.htm |title = Goa Shipyard Ltd. |access-date = 14 December 2007 |publisher = Global Security.Org}} Goa Shipyard unlike [[Cochin Shipyard]] and [[Hindustan Shipyard]] cannot manufacture big vessels of capacity above 15,000 DWT, the average Deadweight Tonnage (DWT) capacity of a ship worldwide is around 60,000 to 80,000 DWT. A new slipway has been commissioned to take up major repair jobs of ships in the dry dock area. A damage control simulator and two double boom level luffing cranes for heavy lifting have been constructed. ==Military ships built== GSL has built the following ships for military use:{{cite web Sailing vessels === In 1997, GSL built the three-masted [[barque]] [[INS Tarangini|INS ''Tarangini'']] for use as a [[training ship|sail training ship]] for the [[Indian Navy]].A sister ship, [[INS Sudarshini]] was also built in 2011. Both ships are based with the [[Southern Naval Command]] in [[Kochi]]. == Future ships == GSL has been nominated to build the following class of ships for the Indian Navy and [[Indian Coast Guard|Coast Guard]]: === ''Talwar''-class frigates === GSL is building two [[Talwar-class frigate|''Talwar''-class frigate]]s in collaboration with Russia's United Ship Building.{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/defence-ministry-clears-goa-shipyard-limted-to-build-frigates/articleshow/57677853.cms|title=Defence ministry clears Goa Shipyard Limted {{sic|hide=y|reason=misspelling in source title}} to build frigates |work=The Times of India|access-date=2017-03-20}} The two vessels were launched in July 2024 and March 2025, respectively. The first is expected to be delivered in 2026.{{Cite web |date=2024-07-23 |title=First indigenous frigate Triput launched by Goa Shipyard Limited |url=https://www.aninews.in/news/national/general-news/first-indigenous-frigate-triput-launched-by-goa-shipyard-limited20240723182918/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Asian News International|ANI]]}}{{cite press release |title=Second Frigate of Project 1135.6 built by GSL launched |date=2025-03-22 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2114025 |access-date=2025-03-22 |work=}} === Fast Patrol Boats for Indian Army === GSL has bagged an Order of Rs.65 Crore from Indian Army to build 12 fast patrol boats for the surveillance and patrolling at large water bodies. The First Vessel is expected to be delivered by July end of 2021.{{Cite web|author=Newton Sequeira|date=Jun 15, 2021|title=Goa Shipyard Limited to deliver first boat to Army for Pangong Tso patrol by July|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/gsl-to-deliver-first-boat-to-army-for-pangong-tso-patrol-by-july/articleshow/83525276.cms|access-date=2021-07-22|website=The Times of India|language=en}} === Floating Dry Dock === A 4,000 ton [[Dry dock|floating dock]] constructed by Goa Shipyard was acquired by the [[Sri Lanka Navy]] as part of a grant from India, to facilitate repair and maintenance of larger fleet units based at [[Trincomalee]] instead of having to depend dry dock facilities in [[Colombo]].{{cite web |title=Four pacts with India compromise Sri Lanka's sovereignty |url=https://ceylontoday.lk/news/four-pacts-with-india-compromise-sri-lanka-s-sovereignty |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220327220225/https://ceylontoday.lk/news/four-pacts-with-india-compromise-sri-lanka-s-sovereignty |archive-date=27 March 2022 |access-date=29 March 2022 |publisher=ceylontoday.lk}} The dock is classified by the [[Indian Register of Shipping]] which is the first defence-export project for the [[Ship classification society|classification society]]. It was launched on 19 February 2026.{{Cite web |title=Indian Register of Shipping's Overseas Defence Project with Sri Lankan Navy |url=https://maritime-executive.com/corporate/indian-register-of-shipping-s-overseas-defence-project-with-sri-lankan-navy |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=The Maritime Executive |language=en}} ==Other products== * [[Tugboat]] * [[Surface effect ship]]s * [[Hovercraft]] * High-speed aluminium-hulled vessels * [[Pollution control]] vessels * Advanced deep sea [[commercial trawler]]s * [[Fish factory vessel]]s, [[Catamaran]]s *[[Ferry]] ==See also== * [[Cochin Shipyard]] * [[Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers]] * [[Hindustan Shipyard]] * [[Mazagon Dock Limited]] ==References== {{reflist}} == External links == * [https://goashipyard.in/ Website] {{Public Sector Undertakings in India}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Shipbuilding companies of India]] [[Category:Indian Navy]] [[Category:Government-owned companies of India]] [[Category:Fishing boat builders]] [[Category:Companies based in Goa]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Vasco da Gama, Goa]] [[Category:1950s establishments in Portuguese India]] [[Category:Indian organisations established in 1957]] [[Category:1957 establishments in the Portuguese Empire]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 1957]]

It was established in 1957, originally by the colonial government of the Portuguese in India as the "Estaleiros Navais de Goa", to build barges to be used in Goa's growing mining industry, which took off after the establishment of India's blockade of Goa in 1955. In the wake of Portugal's defeat and unconditional surrender to India following the 1961 Indian annexation of Goa, it was requisitioned to manufacture warships for the Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard.

To date it has built 167 vessels, including barges, tugs, landing craft, offshore patrol vessels and other vessels for the Indian Navy and Coast Guard and for export to countries like Yemen.
Goa Shipyard unlike Cochin Shipyard and Hindustan Shipyard cannot manufacture big vessels of capacity above 15,000 DWT, the average Deadweight Tonnage (DWT) capacity of a ship worldwide is around 60,000 to 80,000 DWT.
